style: Resilient, physical side under Sergej Barbarez that leans on experience and a robust spine. Build-up runs through technical midfielders into the box for Dzeko and Tabakovic; dangerous on transitions and from crosses, but can be vulnerable defensively against pace.
recent_form: Qualified for only their second-ever World Cup by beating Italy on penalties in a March playoff. Tabakovic's late equalizer in that decisive tie typified their never-say-die qualification run.

key_players.name: Edin Dzeko
key_players.note: Turned 40 in March; still leads the line (73 goals in 148 caps) and the last active member of the 2014 golden generation, playing club football at Schalke.

key_players.name: Haris Tabakovic
key_players.note: Bundesliga-proven finisher; scored the crucial late goal in the qualification-clinching playoff against Italy.

key_players.name: Sead Kolasinac
key_players.note: Physical, experienced full-back/centre-back providing leadership at the back.

key_players.name: Amir Hadziahmetovic
key_players.note: Combative midfielder who screens the defence and recycles possession.

key_players.name: Nikola Vasilj
key_players.note: St. Pauli keeper expected to be busy as the last line for the underdogs.

historical_news: Beat Italy on penalties in a March 2026 playoff to reach only their second-ever World Cup (first since 2014).
40-year-old Edin Dzeko leads the team, the final active member of the 2014 World Cup golden generation.
Miralem Pjanic retired from football in December 2025, ending an era for the national team.
First team to name its final 26-man World Cup squad (announced May 11, 2026).
Drawn into a difficult Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Romantic underdog narrative around Dzeko's farewell tournament and the dramatic playoff win over Italy, balanced by realism about an aging squad and a tough group; viewed as capable of causing an upset.
